title: Alkali transition metal phosphates and related electrode active materials

report.headline: Dead patent with a future: this expired lithium phosphate cathode patent scores 81/100 (high confidence), but the real opportunity likely sits in new materials or processing, not in copying its claims.
report.what_it_is: This patent covers battery cathode materials made of lithium (or sodium or potassium), a transition metal like iron, and phosphate, mixed with small amounts of other metals, much like the LFP chemistry used in many EVs and home batteries. It reached the end of its full term in July 2022 after the owner kept it alive the whole way.

why_it_died.text: It did not die early. It ran out its full term, and the owner paid every maintenance fee as a large entity, which suggests it was valued to the end. That is why the 'died for money, not merit' part of the score is only middling (7.5/15): time ran out, not interest.

case_for.point: The market for this chemistry family appears large and growing. LFP is one of the two main EV battery chemistries, and new LFP cathode plants are planned in Europe and the U.S.
The patent was influential. It has been cited by 125 later filings, and examiners used it against 78 later applications, which suggests its ideas are central to the field.
Its claims were broad at grant, with 35 claims and a family filed in 8 jurisdictions. That breadth helps explain the top marks for breadth and examiner relevance.
Some companies are still building on it. Eight citing filings date from 2019 on, led by Ionobell, so the technical area appears active.

case_against.point: Momentum around this exact patent appears to be fading. No unrelated owner has filed a citing application since it expired. Only 12 cited it in its final five years or later.
The space appears crowded. The original owner and 42 other owners hold later related patents that may still be in force, so the open ground could be narrower than the expiry suggests.
Big players are already scaling LFP production. A startup selling a me-too cathode powder would likely compete on price against very large plants.

blockers.point: Later patents by the original owner, such as US9269955B2 on manganese phosphates, may still be in force and could cover nearby variations.
42 later patents by other owners in this area may still be in force. Each is worth checking before you pick a specific material or process.
Lithium cells need UN 38.3 testing for shipping and usually UL or IEC safety certification for sale. That adds time and cost.
A new chemical substance may need an EPA premanufacture notice under TSCA before commercial manufacture, especially for novel dopant mixes.
The patent describes the material, not the full manufacturing know-how. Expect to rebuild the process details yourself.

assumption_to_test.assumption: Battery cell makers or pack builders would buy a differentiated doped-phosphate cathode material from a startup instead of buying standard LFP from large incumbent suppliers.
assumption_to_test.why_riskiest: The chemistry family is clearly in demand, but big plants are coming online and this patent's own citation activity is fading. Without a buyer who values something beyond cheap commodity LFP, there is no business.
assumption_to_test.how_to_test: Over two weeks, run 10-15 short calls with cathode buyers at small cell makers, energy storage integrators and battery startups. Ask what they pay for LFP today, which performance gaps they would pay a premium to close (rate, low-temperature behavior, energy density), and whether they would test a sample. Also ask one or two contract powder makers for a rough quote. Count how many say they would test a sample at a stated price. Cost: mostly your time, under $500.

attorney_questions: Which of the owner's later patents, such as US9269955B2, and the 42 examiner-cited patents by other owners may still be in force and close to the specific material we plan to make?
Since the patent family was filed in 8 jurisdictions, are any foreign counterparts or related family members still active in the markets where we would sell?
If we change the dopants or the processing method, what should we document now to support filing our own patents later?
report.disclaimer: Research and triage only, not legal advice. This report is not a patentability, validity or freedom-to-operate opinion. Patent status shown here comes from public records that can lag or be wrong. An expired patent is not the same as free to use: follow-on patents, regulatory exclusivity, trade secrets and standards can still block a product. Confirm with a registered patent attorney before acting.

signals.signal: Strong historical technical influence: the patent was widely built upon and frequently used by examiners as prior art, which suggests it sat close to the core of phosphate cathode development.
The owner kept the patent fully maintained to the end of its term as a large entity, which suggests it held ongoing value for them. It reached full term in 2022.

Recent citing activity is modest and concentrated. Since 2019 only 8 filings cite it, mostly from Ionobell, and no unrelated filings cite it after expiry. Direct follow-on interest in this specific patent is therefore thin, even though the revival score is high.
The broader field of olivine/LFP-type phosphate cathodes appears commercially active. Evidence includes new LFP cathode plant announcements and LFP's large share of EV and storage chemistries.

read.who_is_active: Recent filers citing this patent include Ionobell, Hydro-Québec (魁北克电力公司) and Resonac (株式会社力森诺科); ICL with Shenzhen Dynanonic, and L&F with Mitra Chem, are building LFP cathode capacity.
read.market_read: LFP-family phosphate cathodes appear to be a large and growing commercial segment, with new production capacity planned in Europe and the U.S. However, citations of this particular patent have tapered off, so any opportunity likely lies in differentiated materials or processing rather than in this patent's own claims, and this is not a freedom-to-operate assessment.

web.finding: ICL signed a joint venture with Shenzhen Dynanonic to build an LFP cathode material production facility in Europe (Spain).
L&F plans a 15,000-ton LFP cathode materials plant in the U.S. with local partner Mitra Chem, targeting mid- to low-priced battery and energy storage markets.

The IEA Global EV Outlook 2026 says high-nickel and LFP chemistries together make up the vast majority of today's EV battery market, and that record-low LFP prices helped lower overall battery prices.
A trade outlet says that by 2025, 70% of cathode materials will be LFP, driven by use in EVs and stationary storage.
